$comment: The negation engine, lifted from apps/ai-service/app/profiling/signals.py.
WHAT IT DOES: blanks out the words a negator denies, replacing them with SPACES so the
string keeps its LENGTH and every offset-based reader downstream (city spans, salary
windows, _level_near) is unaffected. It also reports which TOPICS were negated.
WHY IT EXISTS: without it, 'abhi kaam nahi mil raha' becomes availability=immediate and
'VMC nahi chalaya' becomes a VMC operator. Both were measured, not imagined.
$comment_backWords: How many words BEFORE a negator get blanked. Three is the measured Hinglish scope:
'setting nahi aati' (2), 'CNC program editing nahi aata' (3). Wider swallowed the next
clause's subject; narrower missed the compound noun.
$comment_tokenTrim: Stripped from both ends of a token before the negator lookup, so 'nahi,' tokenizes as
'nahi'. Includes the Devanagari danda (।) and both dash widths.
$comment_wordScan: Tokenizer. Non-whitespace runs, so offsets stay exact and reconstructable — the masker
writes spaces back at the SAME indices, which only works if tokens carry real offsets.
$comment_clauseSplit: Clause boundaries: punctuation (incl. the Devanagari danda) plus the contrastive
connectors that start a NEW assertion — 'setting nahi aati, sirf chalata hu'.
A spurious split only ever SHRINKS a negation scope, which is the safe direction.
$comment_negators: Unambiguous negators: never a tag or an affirmation in worker speech.
NOT INCLUDED: bare English 'no'. In this domain it is far more often the ABBREVIATION
('part no. 12', 'drawing no. 45') than a denial, and as a negator it would blank the three
words before it — deleting 'drawing' from a worker who reads drawings. 'nahi' and its
spellings carry the real load in worker replies.
$comment_tagNegators: 'na' / 'ना' are negators ONLY sometimes: Hinglish also uses a CLAUSE-FINAL 'na' as an
affirmative tag ('VMC chalata hu na' = 'I do run VMC, right?'). Treating that as a denial
would delete the very machine the worker just claimed, so 'na' negates only when it is
followed by more words in its clause AND is not sitting right after a verb/copula
(the tag position) — that is what `tagPreceders` lists.
$comment_negatableTopicCues: Which TOPIC a negated cue belongs to. Only cue families whose DENIAL is itself a complete
answer are listed — deliberately NOT machines/role/location/salary, where 'VMC nahi' is a
$comment_negationAnswersTopics: Topics for which a DENIAL is a COMPLETE answer, so the ask is satisfied ('kya training li
hai?' -> 'ITI nahi kiya'; 'kya aata hai?' -> 'setting nahi aati').
Deliberately excludes the essentials (role/machines/current_location) and salary: 'VMC nahi
chalaya' is a denial, not an answer, and closing those asks on it would ship an incomplete
profile SILENTLY — the engine must still ask them.
